name: get_app_information
title: Get App Information for suggestions
description: Reads an app's App Information in Atlas for suggestions, for the newest editable version (else the live one): page general (copyright, primaryCategory, secondaryCategory, gamesSubcategories, secondaryGamesSubcategories, contentRights, release), page ageRating (one entry per question, with its answers), page accessibility (per device, one entry per feature with Apple's meaning, answered Yes or No, and the app's accessibilityUrl in `url`), page appPrivacy (the User Privacy Choices URL, privacyChoicesUrl, per language in `locales`) and page review (contactFirstName, contactLastName, contactPhone, contactEmail, demoAccountRequired, demoAccountName, notes). Each field has its current value, App Store Connect's (`live`) where it differs, its limit, and whether it's locked (the version is in review or live); an unanswered question or feature has value null. Categories, both Games subcategory fields, contentRights and release are picked from `choices`, by id. gamesSubcategories (up to two, comma-separated, e.g. "GAMES_PUZZLE,GAMES_WORD"; "" clears them) can be suggested only while the primary category is GAMES, and secondaryGamesSubcategories (the same, from choices.gamesSubcategories) only while the secondary category is GAMES (`available`). demoAccountRequired is App Review's "Sign-in required", yes or no; demoAccountName is the demo account's user name. The demo account's password is never read or suggested: the person types it in Atlas. accessibilityUrl is one for the whole app (every device), and privacyChoicesUrl is set per language: suggest it with page appPrivacy and that locale. Both are optional full https:// URLs. contentRights is Apple's "{ContentRights.appleQuestion}" (its `question`), for the whole app: third-party content is anything the developer doesn't own, such as fonts, images, sounds or music bundled under a license, or content from other services or other people that the app shows or reaches. Suggest USES_THIRD_PARTY_CONTENT (Apple's "Yes, … and I have the necessary rights") when the project has any and it's licensed or permitted, saying in the reason what it is; the person then confirms the rights in Atlas (`rightsConfirmed`). Suggest DOES_NOT_USE_THIRD_PARTY_CONTENT only when everything the app shows is the developer's own. `suggestions` lists the ones already open with their source. App Store Connect won't create review details without a contact email: when the review contact is empty, suggest it from what the project shows (a support or contact email in the app or its docs, or the git author's name and email), and never make up a phone number. Send suggestions with suggest_fields. Pass `version` with a new version queued with propose_app_version to read it before it's in App Store Connect: its copyright, release and App Review fields start from the version before it and aren't locked, and what suggest_fields sends for them with the same `version` waits with it in Review & Push, as do its categories, both Games subcategories and User Privacy Choices URLs (App Store Connect makes a new app info with the version). contentRights and accessibilityUrl belong to the app, not to a version: they're never locked, and with `version` they're suggested for the app as without, not queued with the new version.

name: get_in_app_events
title: Get In-App Events
description: Reads an app's In-App Events from App Store Connect, all of them or one (`eventId`), with the parts you ask for (`include`: texts, media, mediaDetails, review, deepLinkCheck, design, push, queued, or all). Without include, every part but the two heaviest, mediaDetails and design: `leftOut` names them, ask for them when you need them (with eventId to keep the answer small). Each event comes with its id, reference name, badge, state, dates, primaryLocale, deepLink, purpose and priority (null when App Store Connect has none), purchase requirement, and its texts per language (name ≤30 characters, shortDescription ≤50, longDescription ≤120). `missingLanguages` are the store page's languages the event isn't written in yet (people there see the primary language), less those with a suggestion waiting (`suggestedLanguages`; `openSuggestions` has each with its texts, who sent it (`by`; a revision of a written language has `revision: true` and `revises`, only the texts it changes). Reading settles the suggestions as In-App Events does: one whose texts App Store Connect has already is done and leaves, and a new language's texts sent before that language was written become a revision of the texts that differ, its why starting "Suggested before this language was written:"; `stale` and `staleSuggestions` name any left that would add nothing (withdraw your own with withdraw_event_texts) or texts waiting in Review & Push (`queuedTexts`: per language, its changeId(s), newLanguage when the push creates it, waitingForAcceptance, by, and the queued name, shortDescription and longDescription). Only events with `editable: true` take new texts. `media` says, per language, whether it has its own card (16:9) and details page (9:16), as an image or a video, or shows the primary language's; `mediaDetails` has the same per language and kind as App Store Connect gives it (fileName, fileSize, isVideo, width, height, previewFrameTimeCode, imageUrl, state, shownFrom when it's the primary language's), with `atlasFile` when it was uploaded from a file Atlas still has, `matchesQueued` the queued changes sending that same file, and `sameAsPrimary` on a language's own copy of the primary's; `stillMissing` lists what no language shows yet (both are needed to submit the event) and the languages without their own; `queuedArtwork` is art waiting in Review & Push, each with the file Atlas will send: `path` on this Mac (open it to see exactly what goes), `fileSize`, `width`/`height`, a video's `seconds` and `previewFrameTimeCode`, `fileExists`, `languageCreatedByPush` when its language is created by the same push, the file's `originalName`, `sha256` and `origin` (from: makeTheArtwork with conceptId and title, render_event_artwork with page, upload or imageBase64 with name, chooseFiles), `sameAsPrimary` when it's the primary language's art again (with `copyNeeded` false where the language shows the primary's without it: those are in `identicalCopies` for the person to take out), `alreadyInAppStoreConnect` when that language has this file already, and `pushStatus` while a push has it. `queuedArtworkSummary` groups the queued art by kind and file with its languages. `pushInProgress` is true while Review & Push is pushing; `pushChanges` are this app's In-App Event changes in that push (or the one just finished) with their status: queued, sending (progress), done, failed (reason), conflict or notSent (reason). `queued` are the new events waiting in Review & Push, not created yet: their reference names are taken too. `artworkUpload` is this launch's link for sending a card or details page file made elsewhere (POST the bytes, `?name=` the file name). `design` is what the art is designed from: the app's look and design language, what Atlas knows of the app, its design project if one is connected, and `how` to make each piece as an HTML page Atlas renders, still or as a seamless loop. `missingForReview` lists what App Store Connect still needs before it takes the event to App Review (deepLink, primaryLocale, purpose, dates, primaryTexts, languageTexts, card, details, linkNotClaimed), each `missing`, `queued` in Review & Push or `suggested` (waiting for the person to accept it), with `readyForReview`; `queuedDetails` are the deep link, purpose, priority and primary language changes waiting; `deepLinkClaim` says whether the app's project (its folder in Atlas) declares the deep link's URL scheme or applinks domain; `deepLinkCheck` is the last report_deep_link_check for the deep link the event will have (null when not checked), `stale: true` with `staleReason` once the event's start or end moved since it was made (`checkedDates`): check it again. Dates (showsFrom, starts, ends) are as App Store Connect has them, checked at the time you read: missingForReview also lists a date App Store Connect would refuse (publishStartPassed and eventStartPassed: it only takes dates in the future; eventEndBeforeStart, eventTooShort, eventTooLong, publishStartAfterEventStart, publishStartTooEarly), each with `fix` and, for the card's date, `suggested` (a publishStart that works, ISO 8601); `reviewWarnings` say when App Review (up to 2 days; the event shows only once it's approved) may not approve it before its card shows (cardShowsSoon) or it starts (eventStartsSoon): they never block. `queuedDates` are dates waiting in Review & Push (`by` who queued them; `suggestion` an assistant's dates waiting beside the person's, to accept or dismiss); `datesEditable` says whether propose_event_details can change them (else `datesNotEditable` says why). Read-only. Follow with propose_event_texts for the missing languages, render_event_artwork and propose_event_artwork for the art, propose_event_details for a missing deep link, purpose or primary language or dates to fix, or propose_in_app_event for a new event.

Only suggestions sent by this client are removed; `withdrawn` lists them and `left` the ids that weren't, with why (another assistant's or Atlas's own, already accepted or dismissed by the person, or unknown). A value the person accepted waits in Review & Push and isn't touched. Nothing reaches App Store Connect. A release proposal's id (rp-…, from propose_release_action or list_proposals) withdraws it from the version card too, as withdraw_release_action does: it's listed in `withdrawn` with kind release and its action.
